articles.title: Jeff Bezos consortium set to complete minority stake purchase of Liverpool
articles.summary: Liverpool are set to welcome some new stakeholders including Amazon owner Jeff Bezos.
articles.content:
Jeff Bezos consortium set to complete minority stake purchase of Liverpool

Liverpool are set to welcome some new stakeholders including Amazon owner Jeff Bezos.

Last Update:

Liverpool are set to welcome another group of billionaire investors, with a consortium that includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos reportedly closing in on the purchase of a significant minority stake in the Premier League club.

According to Sky News, Fenway Sports Group (FSG) is preparing to announce the sale of a stake worth around one-third of the club, with a deal potentially being confirmed later this week.

Bezos is expected to join the investor group alongside Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin, while the consortium is led by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal and a former shareholder at Queens Park Rangers.

Liverpool value among highest in the world

The investment would reportedly value Liverpool at around £4.5bn, making it one of the biggest valuations ever attached to a football club.

Bezos, whose personal fortune is estimated by Forbes at more than $280bn, has never previously been linked with a move into football ownership, while Saverin – worth an estimated $32bn – was part of the consortium that unsuccessfully attempted to buy Chelsea in 2022.

The proposed investment comes at a time when football’s financial landscape is under intense scrutiny following FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s abandoned plans to sell a stake in the commercial rights to the World Cup and other major tournaments.

That proposal prompted fierce opposition from several governing bodies and reignited debate over the commercial direction of the sport.

FSG has owned Liverpool since 2010, overseeing one of the club’s most successful periods in modern history, including Premier League and Champions League triumphs.

articles.title: FIFA accused of breaking trust of world ‘through deception’
articles.summary: FIFA have been accused of deception by UEFA, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation.
articles.content:
FIFA accused of breaking trust of world ‘through deception’

FIFA have been accused of deception by UEFA, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation.

Last Update:

UEFA, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation have accused FIFA of breaking the trust of world football “through deception”, piling further pressure on president Gianni Infantino in the wake of the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

In a strongly-worded open letter signed by the presidents and general secretaries of the three confederations, the governing bodies said the controversy surrounding the failed investment plan had become a matter of “the integrity of the game, and the integrity of those elected to lead it.”

FFE would have created a new company to manage the commercial and ticketing rights for FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, with a 21% stake earmarked for sale to private investors.

The proposal was scrapped following widespread opposition, led by UEFA, which has already threatened to boycott FIFA competitions if similar plans are revived.

The letter stopped short of naming Infantino directly but delivered a scathing assessment of FIFA’s leadership.

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned,” the statement read.

“Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it.”

Reports claim the letter should be viewed as an opportunity for Infantino to resign voluntarily and leave office with dignity.

Pressure continues to build on Infantino

The statement comes just days after FIFA accused critics of conducting a “concerted and ongoing effort” to undermine both the organisation and its president.

UEFA, Concacaf and the AFC also criticised FIFA’s handling of last week’s management board meeting in Rabat, Morocco, claiming Infantino excluded FIFA Council members and member associations while summoning only senior FIFA employees.

The confederations argued FIFA’s subsequent apology over the handling of the FFE proposal failed to address the central issue.

“It did not acknowledge that the proposal itself was inherently wrong,” the letter said.

“There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the FIFA World Cup was a profound failure of judgement.

“Not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions FIFA exists to serve.”

Although FIFA has pledged to present a report on the episode at the next FIFA Council meeting, expected in October, the three confederations insist any investigation must be conducted independently.

“It fails to recognise that proper governance in the face of such a profound lack of judgement would require that such a review be conducted by a fully independent third party,” the letter added.

articles.title: Why has the Community Shield between Manchester City and Arsenal been switched from Wembley to Cardiff?
articles.summary: Wembley is in use so the curtain raiser will head down the M4
articles.content:
Why has the Community Shield between Manchester City and Arsenal been switched from Wembley to Cardiff?

Wembley is in use so the curtain raiser will head down the M4

Last Update:

The 2026 Community Shield will not be played at its usual home of Wembley this Sunday with the game instead taking place 150 miles away in Cardiff.

The season’s ‘traditional curtain raiser’, which this year will be contested by FA Cup winners Manchester City and Premier League champions Arsenal, has had to be switched.

Wembley has already been booked and so the teams and fans will re-locate to the Welsh capital.

An FA statement read: “The 2026 FA Community Shield will be played at Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Sunday 16 August.

“The ‘curtain raiser’ for the new football season is traditionally played on the weekend before the Premier League begins.

“Due to alterations to the 2026-27 football calendar, next season’s Premier League will begin over the weekend of Saturday 22 August, and Wembley Stadium connected by EE is unavailable on Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August due to pre-planned concerts.”

Table of Contents

Who is performing at Wembley?

Wembley has already been booked for Canadian singer-songwriter The Weeknd.

The R&B artist, whose real name is Abel Makkonen Tesfaye, will perform in London for five nights, from August 14 to August 19.

It means the FA will again use Cardiff as its base as it did when Wembley was being refurbished.

The statement added: “The Welsh national stadium has a rich history of hosting major football events, including the FA Community Shield on six occasions between 2001 and 2006, and it provides a neutral venue for the competing clubs as well as one of the largest capacities in the United Kingdom for fans to attend.”

Where to watch the Community Shield

Manchester City versus Arsenal kicks off at 3pm on Sunday afternoon.

You can watch it on TNT Sports 1 and stream via HBO Max.

articles.title: Mourinho was the ‘Chosen One’ at Manchester United before backing out and rejoining Chelsea
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho rejected the chance to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United in 2013
articles.content:
Mourinho was the ‘Chosen One’ at Manchester United before backing out and rejoining Chelsea

Jose Mourinho rejected the chance to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United in 2013

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho agreed to replace Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United boss in 2013 before changing his mind and re-joining Chelsea.

The mission of succeeding Ferguson at Old Trafford was one of the most sought after jobs in world football at the time and eventually went to David Moyes, supposedly on Ferguson’s say-so.

But it has now emerged the Scot wasn’t first choice with Mourinho initially accepting the role, only to have a late change of heart.

Speaking as part of the new Mourinho documentary on Netflix, which airs on Tuesday, the Portuguese confirmed: “I go to Chelsea in 2013. But in that period, there is something that nobody knows…

“I think I can say because I don’t hurt anyone with the truth. And I think the objective of the work that we are doing is to tell the truth. When I left Real Madrid, I signed with Manchester United to go to Manchester United after Sir Alex.”

Table of Contents

Ferguson confirms Mourinho was first choice

Ferguson, who won 13 Premier League titles over 26 years at United, was heavily involved in choosing his successor and confirmed: “He was offered the job, yes.

“I sat him down and explained the situation. As far as I was concerned, he was accepting. And then, within hours, it changed.”

Mourinho was coming off a fractious spell at Real Madrid and had the choice between United and a return to Chelsea, where he remained a hero after winning the Premier League in 2005 and 2006.

Ferguson said: “One night, he phoned me and he was crying and he says, ‘Alex, I can’t take it. I’ve given my word to Chelsea and I’m not going to break my word’.

“The reason he gave to me, I could understand, but I was disappointed.”

I did it for love – Mourinho on decision to re-join Chelsea

Mourinho’s second spell at Stamford Bridge was not as groundbreaking as his first but he still clinched a third Premier League title.

He insists he doesn’t regret his decision, adding: “I was of course very flattered because Man United has an incredible appeal. When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Manchester United is very, very close.

“But one thing is love for football, and another thing is love for a certain club. I think this is more powerful than love for football, and fundamentally after Real Madrid, I needed to feel that I’m loved.

“For me to lose the chance to be the coach to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson was dramatic. But I don’t regret because it was a decision I made with my heart.

“’I think it is [Friedrich] Nietzsche (the philosopher) who said something that when you do something for love, you are never doing anything wrong. I did it for love.”

Mourinho did eventually end up at Old Trafford in May 2016 but his influence over the game had waned with the likes of Pep Guardiola, Luis Enrique and Jurgen Klopp changing the face of management.

He won the EFL Cup and the Europa League in his first season in charge before being sacked in December 2018.

Mourinho had spells at Tottenham, Roma, Fenerbahce and Benfica before re-joining Madrid this summer.

articles.title: LaLiga President accuses Infantino of ‘destroying’ football
articles.summary: Gianni Infantino has come under fire once again.
articles.content:
LaLiga President accuses Infantino of ‘destroying’ football

Gianni Infantino has come under fire once again.

Last Update:

LaLiga president Javier Tebas has declared Gianni Infantino’s “time has long since passed”, accusing the FIFA chief of “destroying the very essence” of football as pressure continues to mount over his failed private investment proposal.

Infantino has come under increasing scrutiny after abandoning plans to create a commercial subsidiary that would have allowed private investors to buy stakes in FIFA competitions, including the World Cup.

The FIFA president apologised to member associations this week over how the proposal was handled, but the backlash has intensified, with UEFA, the Football Association and several other governing bodies calling for his resignation.

Speaking to French newspaper Le Monde, Tebas said he believes Infantino’s leadership has run its course.

“For me, Gianni Infantino’s time has long since passed,” he said.

“I’m not saying this because of recent events. I have noticed this style of management for a long time, though everyone else seems to be discovering it only now.

“Gianni Infantino is not someone who contributes to the growth of football. On the contrary, his projects are destroying the very essence of the sport: the national leagues.

“Football is not limited to the elite. For me, the Infantino era is over.”

Tebas also argued that replacing Infantino alone would not be enough, insisting FIFA requires wholesale reform.

“What remains to be seen is when that will take effect and how the succession will unfold,” he added.

“I hope it is not just a matter of swapping out some people for others, but of a genuine overhaul.”

Turbulent week continues for Infantino

The criticism comes during a turbulent week for Infantino, with UEFA confirming a departure payment had been made to a former female employee who is alleged to have been in a relationship with him during his time as UEFA general secretary. Infantino has denied those allegations.

Despite FIFA abandoning its investment plans, UEFA has maintained its threat to boycott future World Cups if similar proposals are revived.

Tebas believes the controversy is symptomatic of wider governance issues within football.

“What is happening does not surprise me,” he said.

“What does surprise me is the reaction of many people who remained silent for years.

“This episode is only the tip of the iceberg of what has been going on within an institution, FIFA, but also more broadly in football, where there are no real governance policies.

“And the problem is not limited to one person; it is about an entire system.

“The old system can persist even when the people change. Let’s hope things truly change, that a new leader arrives, and that new governance is established at FIFA.”

articles.title: Mourinho claims new Real Madrid signing Bernardo Silva in ‘poor physical shape’
articles.summary: Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho says Bernardo Silva is not in good physical condition ahead of the new season.
articles.content:
Mourinho claims new Real Madrid signing Bernardo Silva in ‘poor physical shape’

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho says Bernardo Silva is not in good physical condition ahead of the new season.

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho has urged Bernardo Silva to improve his fitness after revealing the Real Madrid midfielder returned for pre-season “in a poor physical shape.”

Silva made his first appearance for Los Blancos in Saturday’s 2-1 friendly win over Ferencvaros after joining the Spanish giants on a free transfer following the expiry of his Manchester City contract.

The Portugal international came off the bench at half-time in Budapest, but Mourinho admitted the 31-year-old is still some way short of full fitness after his summer break.

“Bernardo is a really important player for us, but the poor guy is another one who benefits from not doing anything when they’re on holiday,” Mourinho said.

“It does him good during his time off to not do anything, so he’s come back in a poor physical shape – he has to improve.”

Mourinho also explained why he altered Silva’s position during the second half, moving him further forward because of concerns over his physical condition.

“Bernardo is a tremendous player,” he added.

“He can help us build up play if he plays deeper, as a No.6 or a No.8.

“But, during the game, I realised he was lacking a little physical strength, so I moved him forward to the No.10 position. He can play in three or four positions.”

Madrid win but work to be done

Goals from Mario Rivas and Carlos Espi secured victory for Real Madrid in Hungary, with Silva making his unofficial debut following his arrival in the Spanish capital.

The midfielder was pleased to get his first minutes under his belt and believes he will be ready by the time Madrid begin their La Liga campaign against Espanyol later this month.

“It’s only the first week, but I’m very happy,” Silva told Real Madrid TV.

“There are still many things to improve, but the most important thing is to gain rhythm to start the season well.

“It’s been a tough first week, but I am very happy to have got going and made my debut for Madrid.”

articles.title: PSG complete signing of Aston Villa defender Lucas Digne
articles.summary: Paris Saint-Germain have confirmed the signing of Lucas Digne.
articles.content:
PSG complete signing of Aston Villa defender Lucas Digne

Paris Saint-Germain have confirmed the signing of Lucas Digne.

Last Update:

Paris Saint-Germain have completed the signing of Aston Villa defender Lucas Digne after triggering the £8.5 million release clause in his contract.

The France international has signed a three-year deal with the European champions, returning to the Parc des Princes more than a decade after his first spell at the club.

Digne spent three years at PSG before leaving for Barcelona in 2016 and returns after eight seasons in the Premier League with Everton and Aston Villa.

“I am very honoured to be returning to Paris Saint-Germain following the wonderful experience I had here more than ten years ago,” Digne said.

“I am particularly impressed by how the club has developed over the years.”

The 33-year-old is expected to provide competition for Nuno Mendes at left-back in Luis Enrique’s squad.

Digne joined Aston Villa from Everton in January 2022 and made a significant contribution during his time at Villa Park, helping the club win last season’s Europa League – their first major trophy since 1996.

His departure makes him the third senior player to leave Villa this summer, following Morgan Rogers’ move to Chelsea and Youri Tielemans’ switch to Manchester United.

PSG, who retained the Champions League last season after defeating Arsenal on penalties in the 2026 final, have strengthened their squad with the addition of the experienced full-back as they bid to defend their European crown once again.

articles.title: Arteta frustrated with another pre-season defeat but insists Arsenal will benefit long-term
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta gives his thoughts after Arsenal's loss to Borussia Dortmund.
articles.content:
Arteta frustrated with another pre-season defeat but insists Arsenal will benefit long-term

Mikel Arteta gives his thoughts after Arsenal's loss to Borussia Dortmund.

Last Update:

Mikel Arteta admitted Arsenal’s 3-2 Emirates Cup final defeat to Borussia Dortmund was frustrating but believes there were still plenty of positives to take from the performance.

The Gunners were beaten at the Emirates Stadium despite producing several encouraging attacking moments, with Arteta pointing to defensive lapses and set-piece issues as the key reasons for the defeat.

“Well, disappointed that we lost the game,” Arteta said.

“Obviously, try to understand and give some context to the game in terms of how we played, how we competed and then who competed in the game and for how long as well.

“And bearing all that in mind, I think there were some poor moments where we were not very recognisable, especially in set-pieces and defending actions and timings that we are normally very efficient in.

“Some other very, very positive attacking combinations, big chances that some of them didn’t finish in anything because of the final pass because they were completely open.

“But, overall, disappointed because you want to win the games in any context and today, we haven’t managed to do that.”

Table of Contents

New signings impress

One player who continued to impress was summer signing Christos Tzolis, who registered another assist to make it three goal contributions in as many pre-season appearances.

“Really strong,” Arteta said when asked about the Greek winger.

“I think he looks fit, he looks confident, he looks sharp.

“He made the assist, he created a penalty, he had another two or three very good moments.

“His work rate is unbelievable so far – very good things.”

New arrival Bruno Guimaraes also received a warm reception from supporters before kick-off following his move from Newcastle United, and Arteta believes the Brazil international will bring more than just quality on the pitch.

“You can see the immediate reaction,” he said.

“I think he describes himself as a warrior.

“I think he’s a warrior with a tremendous quality as well and intuition and leadership and charisma that is going to help us, that is going to really ignite something different in the team.

“I think he’s going to push everybody inside the team as well and that’s the type of player that we need.”

Gunners World Cup stars to return

Arteta also confirmed that Arsenal’s World Cup internationals will all return to training on Monday.

“Tomorrow, everybody’s back,” he said.

“Some of them were two days early and some of them were back today just towards the game, which was great.

“So tomorrow we start again, we have everybody back so I can’t wait.”

Looking ahead to the final stages of pre-season, Arteta is pleased with the progress of his squad, while singling out Ethan Nwaneri for praise.

“It’s a tricky thing,” he added.

“Some of them now have good loads. It’s true that we have been training hard and on top of that playing some minutes, especially in this heat today that you could notice, especially the moment the game opened up a little bit.

“But some of them had some really good games.

“I think Ethan has been brilliant throughout pre-season and I’m really happy with him.”

articles.title: Isak confident Liverpool are building despite Monaco defeat: ‘Today felt better than last game’
articles.summary: Alexander Isak was happy with Liverpool's performance despite losing to Monaco today.
articles.content:
Isak confident Liverpool are building despite Monaco defeat: ‘Today felt better than last game’

Alexander Isak was happy with Liverpool's performance despite losing to Monaco today.

Last Update:

Alexander Isak insists Liverpool are heading in the right direction despite their 3-2 pre-season defeat to Monaco at Anfield on Sunday, with the striker pointing to his own improving sharpness as evidence that the new-look side is finding its rhythm.

Isak opened the scoring in the 16th minute with a composed finish, his second goal in as many pre-season appearances, before a combination with Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead on the half-hour.

Aleksandr Golovin’s penalty and Mika Biereth’s equaliser set the stage for Paris Brunner’s late headed winner that snatched the result for Monaco.

The Swede struck an upbeat tone about his own fitness trajectory when speaking after the match.

“I feel good, I feel good,” he said. “Every game hopefully should take me to a better fitness level, so that’s what I’m working towards. I think today felt better than last game and hopefully the next game feels better than today. That’s what pre-season is for, building, and that’s what we have to keep doing.”

Isak also addressed the slight confusion surrounding Liverpool’s second goal, which both he and Wirtz appeared to claim.

“I think we agreed, me and Flo, that we both got a touch on the ball,” Isak said. “But obviously I don’t know who got the first one or the last one. It felt like I was on the ball. I don’t really know.”

On returning to Anfield in front of the club’s supporters for the first time this summer, Isak was straightforward in his assessment.

“It was good. Really nice to be back at home, back in front of the fans and get some more minutes into the legs. So that felt good.”

Asked about his relationship with new manager Andoni Iraola and the mood inside the dressing room, the striker gave a picture of a group focused on being ready when the Premier League season begins.

“Really good. I feel like the spirit is good in the group and we’re all working hard to make things work. We’re going to make sure that we’re ready for the start.”

Liverpool’s next pre-season outing is away at Crystal Palace on August 12.

articles.title: Maresca: Man City boss hails players but insists ‘real business starts’ now
articles.summary: City ran out winners over Atletico Madrid in Seoul.
articles.content:
Maresca: Man City boss hails players but insists ‘real business starts’ now

City ran out winners over Atletico Madrid in Seoul.

Last Update:

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was full of praise for his players following their 3-1 win over Atletico Madrid to end their pre-season tour, but the Italian insists the “real business starts” now.

City take on rivals Arsenal in the Community Shield next Sunday, and Maresca was left somewhat satisfied by his team’s preparations as two goals from Omar Marmoush – both assisted by the impressive Antoine Semenyo – and a late Rayan Ait Nouri strike gave the Premier League club a 3-1 victory in South Korea.

Jorge Dominguez had earlier given Atletico the lead but it was one of few blemishes in an otherwise promising City performance.

And Maresca admitted as much after the game, singling out particular praise for his wide players.

“Overall, 10th August 2026 a very good test against one of the best teams in Europe,” Maresca said.

“Credit to the players for the effort they have done. From tomorrow pre-season is finished and the real business starts.

“I think [wingers] can play well, but the end product is the most important thing.

“l think the first half was a bit unfair – we created four, five chances. But the difference was inside the box. We didn’t score. The big difference was there.

“But for sure you need a player out wide who can create unbalance, especially when they go one v one.”

As City look to adjust to life without former manager Pep Guardiola, Maresca’s aim to continue the success of his predecessor is no easy task.

However, Maresca, who was a coach at City under Guardiola, has been pleased by what he has seen so far.

“I’m very happy. Especially because the players since we started have been open-minded,” he said.

“They want to understand and want to learn why we do things.

“I know that when you join a new club you try to install new patterns or different ideas, the most important thing is we are getting better.

“But the path is a huge path to improve things. But I can see we are trying what we do in training, and we are getting better at that.”

articles.title: Chelsea play out bad-tempered draw to end pre-season tour
articles.summary: The planned penalty shootout was also cancelled.
articles.content:
Chelsea play out bad-tempered draw to end pre-season tour

The planned penalty shootout was also cancelled.

Last Update:

Chelsea concluded their pre-season tour with an ill-tempered draw with Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim.

There were six goals and seven yellow cards across the 90 minutes as the game ended all square, with the planned penalty shootout called off.

Johor took an early lead against the run of play before Liam Delap levelled from the penalty spot before half-time.

Delap then missed a good chance to add a second for a youthful Blues side, but the forward later atoned for his miss after the break, scoring again from the penalty spot.

However, the game was then turned on its head when Johor netted twice to re-take the lead in the final minutes.

But there was still time for a third Chelsea goal, with Mykhailo Mudryk’s cross being turned into his own net by Antonio Glauder to once again draw Xabi Alonso’s men level.

Throughout the clash, there appeared to be some growing friction between the two sides, caused by a number of late tackles and swipes off the ball.

It culminated in some confusion at the full-time whistle when the penalty shootout that had been scheduled was abruptly cancelled.

The hosts’ players walked off the pitch as the Chelsea players stood around waiting for a decision.

articles.title: Dominant Manchester City trail to Atletico Madrid in Seoul
articles.summary: The Premier League club are preparing to face Arsenal in next weekend's Community Shield clash.
articles.content:
Dominant Manchester City trail to Atletico Madrid in Seoul

The Premier League club are preparing to face Arsenal in next weekend's Community Shield clash.

Last Update:

Manchester City dominated for large spells in their pre-season clash with Atletico Madrid in Seoul but fell behind before half-time.

Jorge Dominguez poked home from a corner to give the LaLiga side the advantage in the South Korean capital.

The goal came three minutes before the break, at the end of a half the Premier League club, under new boss Enzo Maresca, largely controlled.

Defender Josko Gvardiol somehow failed to find the net inside the opening 20 minutes when he headed wide from close range.

Savinho and Tijjani Reijnders also went close to opening the scoring, before Diego Simeone’s men edged in front through Dominguez after Morten Hjulmand had kept things alive from a corner.

It was perhaps the only blemish in an otherwise promising 45 minutes for City as they continue to find their feet in a post-Pep Guardiola era and prepare to face Premier League rivals Arsenal in the Community Shield in a week’s time.

articles.title: Inter Miami pay tribute to absent Lionel Messi after death of his father
articles.summary: Jorge Messi passed away at the age of 68.
articles.content:
Inter Miami pay tribute to absent Lionel Messi after death of his father

Jorge Messi passed away at the age of 68.

Last Update:

Inter Miami has paid tribute to their absent captain Lionel Messi following the death of his father.

Jorge Messi, who was also his son’s agent, passed away aged 68 in his hometown of Rosario, Argentina, on Friday, with his family confirming the news the following day.

As a result, Messi missed his side’s Leagues Cup clash with Monterrey at Nu Stadium, which Miami lost 2-1.

A minute’s silence was observed ahead of kick-off, with Jorge Messi’s name shown on screens inside the venue. Miami players could also be seen wearing black armbands.

In the 10th minute, the number worn by Messi, fans chanted and unveiled flags in support of the 39-year-old, including one that read “Fuerza [stay strong] Leo”.

Miami midfielder Rodrigo De Paul, who captained the team Saturday, honoured his compatriot after opening the scoring in the 32nd minute, when he removed his shirt to reveal a Messi No 10 jersey.

Hugo Cuypers levelled the score shortly after half-time before Diego Rossi netted a 90th-minute winner for the Mexican side to take all three points and put a major dent in Miami’s hopes of reaching the knockout stages of the competition.

It is not yet known when Messi, who arrived in Rosario on Saturday ahead of a reported private memorial service, will return to Miami.

‘Our hearts are with our captain’

Earlier in the day, the MLS club had written: “Our hearts are with our captain, Leo, and the entire Messi family.”

Meanwhile, Luis Suarez, who missed Saturday’s game because of a suspension, also sent a message of support to his teammate and friend.

“Friend, I hug you and your family strongly,” the striker posted on social media.

“Your dad, from above, will continue to watch you with pride like he did always. All my love in these difficult moments to the Messi Family. Rest in peace, Jorge.”

The Messi family had kept details of Jorge’s illness private before revealing during this summer’s World Cup that he was in the process of receiving medical treatment.

After scoring in Argentina’s opening match against Algeria, an emotional Messi admitted his celebration was about more than football.

“I have been through some difficult, complicated days,” he said.

“I am thankful for the support I have received from my teammates and the staff during this time.”

articles.title: Carrick eager to piece full Manchester United squad together as season draws closer
articles.summary: Michael Carrick is looking forward to the new season after Manchester United's 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain.
articles.content:
Carrick eager to piece full Manchester United squad together as season draws closer

Michael Carrick is looking forward to the new season after Manchester United's 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain.

Last Update:

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says he is eager to have his full squad together as preparations for the 2026-27 season enter their final stage.

The Reds drew 1-1 with Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain in their latest pre-season outing, with Bryan Mbeumo continuing his impressive form by scoring his third goal in two matches after cancelling out Ibrahim Mbaye’s early opener.

Several senior players, including Bruno Fernandes, Diogo Dalot, Noussair Mazraoui and Youri Tielemans, returned to action, although Tom Heaton and Mason Mount were both forced off with suspected injuries.

United will now travel to the Republic of Ireland, where Carrick hopes having the entire squad together will help accelerate preparations ahead of the new campaign.

“I’m looking forward to it,” Carrick said.

“It’s been, a little bit, different chapters through pre-season and we’ll get everybody together when we get to Dublin over the next couple of days.

“It’ll be great, two more games this week and, again, I’m looking forward to seeing the group develop.”

Manchester United round off their pre-season schedule with fixtures against Leeds United on Wednesday before taking on AC Milan next Saturday, with Carrick hoping to have his squad fully prepared ahead of the Premier League opener.

articles.title: Pre-season round-up: Tottenham fail to win as Premier League clubs continue preparations
articles.summary: Catch up with the best of the action from Saturday's pre-season action.
articles.content:
Pre-season round-up: Tottenham fail to win as Premier League clubs continue preparations

Catch up with the best of the action from Saturday's pre-season action.

Last Update:

Saturday delivered a busy programme of pre-season action across Europe, with several Premier League sides using the final weeks before the season kicks off to sharpen their preparations. Here is how things unfolded.

Table of Contents

Leeds 2-0 RB Leipzig

The standout result of the day. Daniel Farke’s side produced an emphatic display against last season’s third-placed Bundesliga outfit, winning 2-0 across 120 minutes in front of 24,630 supporters at Elland Road as the club debuted their new home kit for the first time.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin continued his rich pre-season form by opening the scoring inside seven minutes, converting from close range after Joe Rodon drove forward from centre-back and delivered a precise ball across the face of goal.

Lukas Nmecha wrapped up the win in the final stages after a sharp combination involving Brenden Aaronson and Wilfried Gnonto, slotting in at the near post.

Brighton 3-0 Roma

Brighton produced their most convincing performance of pre-season with a three-goal victory over Roma at the Amex, giving Fabian Hurzeler plenty of encouragement on the eve of competitive action.

The Seagulls were fluid and forward-thinking throughout, with the attacking intent that defined their 2025-26 campaign visible from early in the match. Roma, preparing for the new Serie A season, offered limited resistance across 90 minutes.

Brighton’s striker situation remains the one point of discussion heading into the new season, but on the evidence of Saturday, their system has plenty of quality behind the final third.

Ipswich 3-0 Rayo Vallecano

A confidence-boosting result for Gary O’Neil’s promoted side, who hammered La Liga opponents Rayo Vallecano 3-0 at Portman Road to cap their home pre-season programme in style.

After a mixed run of results that included defeats to Osasuna and Oxford United, the manner and scoreline of this victory was exactly what Ipswich needed.

The result comes after a 1-0 win over Le Havre four days earlier and suggests the squad is hitting form at the right time. O’Neil will have been particularly pleased with the defensive organisation on display against technically capable Spanish opposition.

Tottenham 1-1 Getafe

A useful if inconclusive workout for Roberto De Zerbi’s Spurs at their Hotspur Way training ground. The match was shortened to 70 minutes behind closed doors, with Getafe breaking the deadlock in the 66th minute when Alberto Risco cut inside and finished past Antonin Kinsky.

Conor Gallagher levelled four minutes later with a surging central run and low diagonal finish into the far corner. Spurs remain unbeaten in pre-season after their 2-1 victory over Chelsea in Sydney.

Stuttgart 3-1 Everton

A difficult afternoon for Everton in Stuttgart, with the Toffees beaten 3-1 by the Bundesliga side in a result that will give their management pause for thought.

Everton had been building some momentum, a 2-1 win over Hamburg was a positive marker, but were second best for most of the match in Germany.

The scoreline flatters the visitors slightly given the control Stuttgart maintained across the second half. Everton face Newcastle in Edinburgh next on their pre-season schedule and will want a sharper showing.

Frankfurt 2-0 Hull

A tough afternoon in Germany for Hull City, beaten 2-0 by Eintracht Frankfurt in what was their sternest pre-season test to date. The promoted side have found results mixed since pre-season began, and Frankfurt’s intensity and technical quality proved too much to handle across 90 minutes. Li

Nottingham Forest 0-1 Udinese & 0-1 Barcelona

A chastening day in Italy for Forest, who played back-to-back matches in the Friuli Cup in Udine and lost both.

Udinese beat them 1-0 in the opening fixture of the afternoon, and then Barcelona followed up with a 1-0 victory in the second match at the same venue, completing a double blow for Oliver Glasner’s side.

Real Betis 2-2 Bournemouth

Bournemouth’s three-match winning run came to an end in Seville, where they were held to a 2-2 draw by a Betis side in impressive pre-season form.

Manuel Pellegrini’s team had beaten Arsenal 3-1 in their previous friendly and carried that confidence into a lively contest at La Cartuja.

Bournemouth, who had hammered Augsburg 5-2 and thrashed Genoa 10-1 behind closed doors earlier in the summer, showed enough to suggest their attacking depth remains a genuine strength, but were unable to hold on for a win against La Liga opposition.

Valencia 1-2 Newcastle

A positive result for Matthias Jaissle’s Newcastle, who came from behind to beat Valencia 1-2 at the Mestalla in the evening’s late kick-off.

Midfielder Ugrinic gave the La Liga side the lead and the match looked to be heading Valencia’s way before Newcastle rallied to score twice and claim what was only their second win of an otherwise difficult pre-season programme.

articles.title: Alonso reveals how Chelsea will deliver success after impressive win over AC Milan
articles.summary: Xabi Alonso says flexible tactics will be the key to Chelsea's success this season.
articles.content:
Alonso reveals how Chelsea will deliver success after impressive win over AC Milan

Xabi Alonso says flexible tactics will be the key to Chelsea's success this season.

Last Update:

Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso believes tactical flexibility will be key to his side’s success after watching the Blues cruise to a 3-0 victory over AC Milan to lift the Indonesia Super Cup.

Joao Pedro scored twice in Jakarta to continue his impressive pre-season form, while Moises Caicedo also found the net as Chelsea delivered another encouraging display ahead of the new campaign.

Alonso’s side regularly shifted shape throughout the contest, with players interchanging positions in and out of possession, and the Spaniard says that versatility is central to the way he wants his team to play.

“We want to be versatile in our approach and system,” Alonso said.

“I think we have the players to adapt to different ones because they understand how to support each other.

“The principles are the same but the movements can change; we need to be unpredictable, we want to be flexible, and we want to have a threat.

“The system is just a picture; you need to move, rotate and create dynamics and that is when the picture becomes a movie.

“We are not just sticking to one idea and the more options that we have, the better team we will be.”

Chelsea now head into the final game of their pre-season tour against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia before turning their attention to the start of the Premier League season.

Alonso is pleased with the progress his squad has made so far but insists there is still plenty of room for improvement.

“In pre-season, we have a few games already and for sure, the more players we have available, the more options we have,” he added.

“I think that we will get better and by the start of the Premier League season we will be ready.

“But even that will be another starting point in the evolution of the team. So it will be a process that takes months and in every game.”

articles.title: Lionel Messi’s father Jorge dies aged 68
articles.summary: Lionel Messi's father, Jorge, has passed away at the age of 68.
articles.content:
Lionel Messi’s father Jorge dies aged 68

Lionel Messi's father, Jorge, has passed away at the age of 68.

Last Update:

Lionel Messi’s father and long-time agent, Jorge Messi, has died at the age of 68 following a prolonged illness.

Jorge passed away in hospital in his hometown of Rosario, Argentina, on Friday, with the family confirming the news on Saturday.

The Messi family had kept details of his illness private before revealing during this summer’s World Cup that he was receiving medical treatment.

After scoring in Argentina’s opening match against Algeria, an emotional Messi admitted his celebration was about more than football.

“I have been through some difficult, complicated days,” he said.

“I am thankful for the support I have received from my teammates and the staff during this time.”

A week later, the family released a statement confirming Jorge’s condition.

“The Messi family informs that Jorge Messi is currently going through a health situation.

“At this time, he is under medical supervision, recovering and progressing favourably within the condition he is experiencing.”

Messi legacy lives on

Jorge is survived by his wife, Celia, and their four children: Lionel, Rodrigo, Matias and María Sol.

Messi’s boyhood club, Newell’s Old Boys, led the tributes.

“Newell’s Old Boys mourn with profound pain and sorrow the passing of Jorge Messi,” the club said.

“He was a renowned Newell’s supporter, businessman and the father of the captain of the Argentina national team, Lionel Messi.

“Jorge was the support and the person who, together with his wife, Celia, strengthened the career of the greatest player of all time with vision, rigour and affection.

“His constant support and behind-the-scenes leadership were fundamental in supporting every step of Lionel’s journey.”

Jorge worked in a steel factory in Rosario before moving to Europe when Messi joined Barcelona’s academy in 2000.

He went on to oversee his son’s career as his agent, guiding moves from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain and later Inter Miami, while helping manage one of the most successful careers in football history.

articles.title: Joao Pedro gives Chelsea half-time advantage against AC Milan in Indonesia
articles.summary: Joao Pedro was on target as Chelsea took a 1-0 lead into half-time against AC Milan in Jakarta
articles.content:
Joao Pedro gives Chelsea half-time advantage against AC Milan in Indonesia

Joao Pedro was on target as Chelsea took a 1-0 lead into half-time against AC Milan in Jakarta

Last Update:

Chelsea had the better of the opening 45 minutes against AC Milan in Jakarta and were rewarded by Joao Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

Pedro, who had not scored in either of Chelsea’s last two games after netting a hat-trick as a substitute against the Western Sydney Wanderers on July 28, broke the deadlock in the second minute of injury-time, nodding an inswinging corner past Milan goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriani at the far post.

Ruben Amorim’s Milan bossed the ball in the early stages with the tempo dictated by evergreen midfielder Luka Modric but it was Chelsea who conjured up the opening chance, Pedro’s shot deflected wide after the Brazilian latched on to a free-kick from Pedro Neto.

Pedro threatened again after 13 minutes with a low shot that was well saved by young Milan keeper Torriani.

Danny Welbeck fired wide before Milan had their first moment as an attacking threat with Christian Comotto seeing a shot blocked after Robert Sanchez’s punch fell to him on the edge of the area.

Torriani was the busier of the two keepers in the opening half hour and he produced another good stop to prevent Neto’s curling effort creeping into the far corner. But there was little he could do when Pedro was left unmarked and guided a downward header into the net.

Table of Contents

CHELSEA TEAM NEWS

Alonso made four changes to the side beaten by Juve with Josh Acheampong, Romeo Lavia, Cole Palmer and Neto coming in for Tosin Adarabioyo, Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, Geovany Quenda and Jamie Gittens.

Chelsea: Sanchez; Palestra, Acheampong, Fofana, Hato; Caicedo, Lavia, Palmer, Joao Pedro, Neto; Welbeck

Chelsea Substitutes: Sharman-Lowe, Penders, Sarr, Anselmino, Tosin, Subuloye, Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Watson, Walsh, Satpayev, Quenda, Gittens, Estevao, Mudryk, Jackson, Delap

AC MILAN TEAM NEWS

Christian Pulisic has a thigh problem and Mike Maignan is still working his way back into full training after his World Cup commitments.

Modric started as did former Chelsea star Ruben Loftus-Cheek.

AC Milan: Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlovic; Modric, Comotto, Loftus-Cheek, Estupinan; Chukwueze, Leao; Camarda

AC Milan Substitutes: to follow

articles.title: BREAKING: Arsenal confirm signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle
articles.summary: Arsenal have bolstered the squad that won the Premier League title last season by signing Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle
articles.content:
BREAKING: Arsenal confirm signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle

Arsenal have bolstered the squad that won the Premier League title last season by signing Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle

Last Update:

Arsenal have completed the signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75million.

The Brazil midfielder has signed a four-year deal at the Emirates with the option for a further 12 months and ends a protracted saga with Newcastle eventually admitting defeat in their bid to keep their captain.

Guimaraes joined Newcastle in January 2022 for £42m and made 153 Premier League appearances, scoring 30 goals and adding 26 assists. His former club Lyon are due 20 per cent of the profit Newcastle will make on the player.

Table of Contents

Guimaraes posts emotional message to Newcastle after leaving for Arsenal

His exit is another blow to Newcastle who have already lost key players Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer. Gordon went to Barcelona while Tonali opted to join Tottenham for combined fees in the region of £170m.

But losing Guimaraes will cut particularly deep for Newcastle fans.

He said: “This is one of the toughest decisions of my life. When I arrived, the club was in a challenging position and I am incredibly proud of what we achieved together.

“I fell in love with this place. I really mean that. From my first day, the supporters, my teammates, Eddie [Howe] and the staff, and everyone connected with the club made me and my family feel at home.

“This move is very tough because Newcastle means so much to me, but I wanted to experience something new in my life. I feel ready for a new challenge for myself and my family.

“I had a very positive conversation with [new coach] Matthias Jaissle, and I leave knowing the club is in very good hands.

“To the supporters, thank you will never be enough, but I say it with all my heart. I will always be proud to have been part of this club’s journey. Thank you for everything.”

Guimaraes will add to Arsenal’s deep midfield reserves

Arsenal already boast arguably the best midfield in the Premier League with the likes of Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, Martin Zubimendi and Eberechi Eze having helped them to the title last season.

But Gunners sporting director Andrea Berta believes the signing of Guimaraes will provide boss Mikel Arteta with another option.

He told the club’s official website: “We are delighted to welcome Bruno Guimaraes to our club.

“Bruno is a player with a great mentality and great quality, who will bring strong leadership to our squad.

“With Bruno joining us, we are further strengthening the heart of our team. As we have all seen, Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity, and has provided goals and assists for his team every year.

“Bruno will allow Mikel to further develop our playing style and will also increase our internal competitiveness, which is essential for maintaining the standards required when we are aiming to win major trophies.”

Guimaraes targets trophies with Arsenal

Guimaraes helped Newcastle claim their first piece of domestic silverware in 70 years when they won the 2025 EFL Cup and he is hoping to add to his collection in North London.

“It’s massive what I have done so far, but I want more,” he said. “I want to win for Arsenal. I want to win more trophies in my career, and I think I’m in the right place, at my peak at 28 years old.

“I’m so excited to join. Here, wearing this shirt, you have to go for winning trophies, winning everything we can and make history.

“I want to put my name in the club history. Someday, when I leave, I want players to come here and say I want to do exactly what Bruno did for the club.

“I think it’s the best thing that a player can do for the club: create history and inspire the young.”

articles.title: Liverpool agree to sign Barcelona defender Araujo on loan
articles.summary: Liverpool are adding Ronald Araujo to their backline this season.
articles.content:
Liverpool agree to sign Barcelona defender Araujo on loan

Liverpool are adding Ronald Araujo to their backline this season.

Last Update:

Liverpool have agreed a loan deal to sign Ronald Araujo from Barcelona, according to Fabrizio Romano.

Romano reported that a verbal agreement has been reached club to club and has been approved by Barcelona sporting director Deco, with a loan deal including an option to buy now in place.

Personal terms between the player and Liverpool are also understood to have been agreed.

The move comes as a direct response to an injury crisis at the back that has left new manager Andoni Iraola with precious little cover heading into the start of the Premier League season.

Ibrahima Konate left for Real Madrid on a free transfer at the end of his contract. Jeremy Jacquet, signed from Rennes for £55 million, is still working his way back from a shoulder injury.

Giovanni Leoni, recruited as a long-term defensive partner for Virgil van Dijk, suffered an ACL tear and will miss the opening months of the campaign entirely. Joe Gomez sustained a further setback during the 4-2 pre-season win over Sunderland.

The situation has left Liverpool, in effect, without a fit and available senior centre-back in the immediate term, and the Araujo deal addresses that emergency.

Liverpool move for experience

The Uruguayan is 27 years old, stands at 6ft 3in and has spent seven seasons at the Camp Nou since joining Barcelona B from Boston River in 2018.

He made 162 appearances for the Catalan club across all competitions during that period, winning two La Liga titles in 2022-23 and 2024-25, and has also shown the versatility to operate at right-back when required.

Last season, however, his role at Barcelona diminished significantly. He started just 11 of his 24 La Liga appearances as Pau Cubarsi, Eric Garcia and Gerard Martin were all preferred at various stages, contributing three goals from set pieces but ultimately losing his status as a guaranteed starter under Hansi Flick.

Injury has been the persistent theme of his Barcelona career. He suffered a serious adductor tendon injury in September 2022 that ruled him out of the World Cup in Qatar, a knee problem at the end of last season, an ankle injury in February 2025 and an illness-related absence in November 2025.

articles.title: ‘None of us wanted to sell Bruno’ – Wilson admits Guimaraes exit was not part of Newcastle’s plans
articles.summary: Newcastle's sporting director said there were no plans to sell club captain Bruno Guimaraes this summer.
articles.content:
‘None of us wanted to sell Bruno’ – Wilson admits Guimaraes exit was not part of Newcastle’s plans

Newcastle's sporting director said there were no plans to sell club captain Bruno Guimaraes this summer.

Last Update:

Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson has admitted the club had no intention of selling captain Bruno Guimaraes this summer, despite the Brazilian midfielder edging closer to a £75 million move to Arsenal.

The 28-year-old has not been officially confirmed as an Arsenal player but a deal is understood to have been agreed between the two clubs, with Guimaraes set to become the latest high-profile departure from St James’ Park in what has been a turbulent few months for the Magpies.

Newcastle have already lost Anthony Gordon to Barcelona and Sandro Tonali to Tottenham during the window, while Eddie Howe’s resignation last week added further upheaval to a club in a period of significant transition. Matthias Jaissle was formally appointed as head coach on Wednesday.

Speaking to reporters from Newcastle’s pre-season training base in Spain, Wilson was candid about the circumstances surrounding Guimaraes’ departure.

“We didn’t want to sell Bruno. It wasn’t in the plan to sell Bruno. None of us, or ownership, wanted to sell Bruno,” he said.

“He’s our captain, he was very, very important to us and the debate over his price — it’s a world-record fee for a player of his age.

“What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, effectively told us he wanted to leave and move on.

“That doesn’t mean he can go but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number. But there’s no part in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer – it wasn’t.

“But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen. It might have been in our plan to sign one player but we didn’t get him so we move on to another. We can only be honest about that.”

articles.title: Argentina: No pressure on Messi to play 2028 Copa America
articles.summary: Lionel Messi will not be pressure into playing for Argentina in the 2028 Copa America.
articles.content:
Argentina: No pressure on Messi to play 2028 Copa America

Lionel Messi will not be pressure into playing for Argentina in the 2028 Copa America.

Last Update:

Argentina will not pressure Lionel Messi into playing at the 2028 Copa America, with Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia insisting the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner will decide his own international future.

Messi, 39, has yet to announce his plans after inspiring Argentina to the 2026 World Cup final, scoring eight goals and providing four assists during the tournament.

“It’s entirely his decision,” Tapia said. “He has to feel like playing. In 2022, we didn’t know if he would be at the 2026 World Cup, but he took it one match at a time and showed his best level once again.”

The Inter Miami forward has enjoyed an extraordinary international career, making a record 207 appearances for Argentina while scoring 125 goals.

He has won two Copa America titles and the 2022 World Cup, as well as being named player of the tournament in Qatar.

“We should be proud of him,” Tapia added. “May he continue enjoying football, and may he make the decision he believes is right.”

Scaloni to be offered new contract

Tapia also revealed he is determined to keep Lionel Scaloni as Argentina head coach beyond the end of his current contract, which expires later this year.

Scaloni admitted after Argentina’s extra-time defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final that he would take time to consider his future.

“My plan A, plan B and plan C is Scaloni,” Tapia said. “I want him to stay and we all want him to stay, but I have to respect whatever decision he makes.”

Scaloni has become Argentina’s most successful coach since taking charge in 2018, guiding the national team to Copa América triumphs in 2021 and 2024, as well as World Cup glory in 2022.

articles.title: Chelsea star issues Xabi Alonso verdict: ‘I don’t care about the system’
articles.summary: Xabi Alonso will manage in the Premier League for the first time
articles.content:
Chelsea star issues Xabi Alonso verdict: ‘I don’t care about the system’

Xabi Alonso will manage in the Premier League for the first time

Last Update:

Chelsea’s squad are “so happy” with Xabi Alonso as the new head coach attempts to revive the club’s fortunes, new defender Marco Palestra says.

Right-back Palestra, who became one of eight signings made by Alonso this summer when the 21-year-old arrived for £47 million from Atalanta in July, believes the Spaniard’s preferred slow and patient passing style and vigorous pursuit of turnovers can transform the 10th-placed side in last season’s Premier League.

“I’m sure that if we follow the idea of Xabi and we improve every day, we can have a big season,” said Italy international Palestra.

“Chelsea is one of the best teams in the world, so [success] is normal for Chelsea.”

Table of Contents

Chelsea squad ‘follow Alonso ideas’

Alonso established himself as one of the best young managers in the world by winning a domestic treble with Leverkusen in 2023/24, but his switch to Real Madrid last season proved brief and unsuccessful.

Among Alonso’s signings, the former Bayern, Real Madrid and Liverpool midfielder has spent £117m to bring in Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa and £52m to recruit Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace.

“Not only me, but all my teammates are so happy to be managed by Xabi Alonso,” said Palestra. “So we are happy and all thinking about becoming better every day.

“The system is good but I don’t care about the system. Xabi knows better than me and we follow his ideas.”

Marco Palestra: Chelsea ‘one of the best clubs’

Atalanta youth product Palestra barely featured for La Dea’s first team but impressed on loan at Cagliari last season.

“I’m really confident,” he said. “For sure it’s a big move, but I played [regulary] in Serie A, and Serie A is difficult to play in.

“I need to say thank you to the staff, Xabi and my teammates because, since the first day, they’ve helped me with everything inside and outside of football.

“I chose Chelsea because it’s one of the best clubs in football. [Alonso] gave me a lot confidence.”

Chelsea: Xabi Alonso on Marco Palestra

Alonso praised Palestra’s “great impact” after Chelsea’s 1-0 defeat to Juventus in Hong Kong on Wednesday

“You see his power,” said the 44-year-old. “He repeats [his runs] up and down, [showing] big stamina and quality in the last third.

“We are impressed with him and happy that we have Marco in the squad and that he gives solutions. He’s a flexible player, so it’s going to be very interesting to work with him.”

articles.title: Manchester City demand £68m after rejecting opening Barcelona bid for Rodri
articles.summary: Manchester City have knocked back an opening bid for Rodri from Barcelona.
articles.content:
Manchester City demand £68m after rejecting opening Barcelona bid for Rodri

Manchester City have knocked back an opening bid for Rodri from Barcelona.

Last Update:

Manchester City have rejected an opening £38.5m bid from Barcelona for Rodri as the Spanish champions step up their pursuit of the midfielder.

Barcelona made their first formal offer on Friday after receiving the player’s approval to open negotiations, but City value the 30-year-old at more than £60m and are unwilling to sell for the initial proposal.

Rodri has entered the final year of his contract at the Etihad Stadium and is yet to agree an extension, fuelling speculation over his future throughout the summer.

Real Madrid had long been viewed as the favourites to sign the Spain international, but talks with the European champions have now ended, leaving Barcelona at the front of the queue.

Although Barca sources previously suggested there was no guarantee a deal would materialise, discussions with Rodri’s representatives remain ongoing after the club submitted their opening bid.

The Ballon d’Or winner endured an injury-hit 2024-25 campaign after suffering a serious knee injury before later being sidelined by a hamstring problem.

However, Rodri returned to his best at this summer’s World Cup, helping Spain lift the trophy and being named player of the tournament.

He is currently recovering from back surgery and is expected to rejoin City’s squad in Manchester early next week.

articles.title: England striker Toney charged with assault
articles.summary: England striker Ivan Toney will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on September 24
articles.content:
England striker Toney charged with assault

England striker Ivan Toney will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on September 24

Last Update:

England striker Ivan Toney has been charged with assault causing actual bodily harm following an incident in a London nightclub last December.

Toney, who plays for Saudi Arabian club Al-Ahli, was involved in an altercation on Wardour Street in Soho and will appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on September 24.

A spokesperson for the 30-year-old said in remarks reported by the BBC: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”

Toney was a member of England’s World Cup squad and started the 3rd/4th play-off against France, a game the Three Lions won 6-4 in Miami.

His only other appearance at the tournament was as a last-gasp substitute as England tried to find a late equaliser in the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Northampton-born Toney moved to Saudi Arabia in 2024 after a prolific spell at Brentford for whom he scored 67 goals in 128 appearances.

articles.title: Manchester United offload another goalkeeper as Bayindir sent on loan to Celta Vigo
articles.summary: Altay Bayindir will spend next season in Spain with Celta Vigo after failing to make an impression at Manchester United
articles.content:
Manchester United offload another goalkeeper as Bayindir sent on loan to Celta Vigo

Altay Bayindir will spend next season in Spain with Celta Vigo after failing to make an impression at Manchester United

Last Update:

Manchester United goalkeeper Altay Bayindir will spend next season on loan at Celta Vigo.

The Turkey international has struggled to make an impression at Old Trafford after joining from Fenerbahce in 2023. He started last season as United’s number one but returned to a back-up role due to the emergence of Senne Lammens.

He is the second United goalkeeper to be farmed out this summer with Andre Onana moving on a second successive season-long loan to Trabzonspor, where he will play with Mohamed Salah.

A United statement read: “Manchester United goalkeeper Altay Bayindir has agreed to join La Liga side Celta Vigo on loan for the duration of the 2026/27 season, subject to registration.

“The 28-year-old played six games for United last season, his third term since joining from Fenerbahce in 2023. Following his debut against Newport County in 2024, Altay has made 17 appearances in total for the club.

“Bayindir now heads out to Spain to link up with Os Celestes, who finished sixth in La Liga last season under head coach Claudio Giraldez and are set to compete in this season’s Europa League.”

United rejig goalkeeping stocks

Lammens is firmly established as the number one under Michael Carrick with new signing Karl Darlow and the veteran Tom Heaton also available as options. Radek Vitek, who spent last season on loan at Bristol City, is expected to join Middlesbrough in the coming days.

United face Paris Saint-Germain in a friendly in Gothenburg tomorrow. They start their Premier League campaign at newly promoted Hull on Saturday, August 22.

articles.title: Rodri gives green light to Barcelona move in major snub for Real Madrid
articles.summary: Manchester City midfielder Rodri has performed a u-turn and indicated he would rather join Barcelona than Real Madrid
articles.content:
Rodri gives green light to Barcelona move in major snub for Real Madrid

Manchester City midfielder Rodri has performed a u-turn and indicated he would rather join Barcelona than Real Madrid

Last Update:

Barcelona are actively working on bringing in Rodri after the Manchester City midfielder gave the green light to a move to Catalonia.

Barca have made tentative enquiries to the player’s camp over the past few days to discover the extent of his desire to move to Camp Nou after previous reports indicated he had his heart set on a switch to Real Madrid.

And they discovered Rodri was eager to join Hansi Flick’s side and link up again with many of the players that worked together to help Spain win the World Cup.

It is a major blow for Madrid, who had assumed the 30-year-old would be the next piece of their jigsaw as they attempt to wrestle back the Liga title under Jose Mourinho.

The signing yesterday of 19-year-old winger Yan Diomande and the announcement that Vinicius Jr had renewed his contract at the Santiago Bernabeu was overshadowed slightly by the fact one of their key targets had snubbed them for their arch-rivals.

A fee of around €60million (£51.4m) would be enough to secure the player, who has less than 12 months left on his deal at City with the Premier League club aware of Rodri’s desire to return to Spain.

Mundo Deportivo report Rodri would like the matter resolved before he returns to City on August 13.

Table of Contents

De Jong injury forces Barcelona to seek midfielders

Rodri would fit in perfectly at Camp Nou given Barca’s style of play is similar to that employed by both City and Spain. He won the 2024 Ballon d’Or and was awarded the Golden Ball for best player at the 2026 World Cup after captaining Spain to the title.

Barca are exploring the possibility of bringing him to Catalonia due to doubts over the fitness of Netherlands midfielder Frenkie de Jong.

De Jong suffered a tear of the MCL in his right knee at the World Cup but opted against surgery, preferring a ‘conservative method of treatment’, albeit that may change depending on his progress.

If an operation is required then De Jong would be sidelined for several months, leaving Barca a man light in a key position.

What has Rodri said about a possible move back to Spain?

Rodri, who is currently recovering from a minor back operation, has flirted with the idea of moving back to his homeland for several months. However, all the talk was about a deal with Madrid, not Barcelona.

He said in March: “Having played for Atlético [in 2018-19] before would not prevent me from playing for Real Madrid. There are other players who have done that before. Maybe not direct transfers, but eventually. You can’t turn down one of the world’s best clubs.”

His departure would be a major blow to new City boss Enzo Maresca.

Speaking in his first press conference as City boss last month, Maresca expressed calm over the speculation.

“First of all, we have to say that around big players there is always speculation,” Maresca said.

“So I’m not worried about that, it’s normal, also because they [Spain] won the World Cup – he is one of the best players.

“I think every manager wants to have Rodri, because he’s a top player.

“But now, surgery [on a back problem], and then he needs holiday, he needs to rest, recovery, and then he will be back here with us.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Vinicius Junior signs Real Madrid contract until 2032
articles.summary: Vinicius Junior has signed a five-year extension at Real Madrid
articles.content:
BREAKING: Vinicius Junior signs Real Madrid contract until 2032

Vinicius Junior has signed a five-year extension at Real Madrid

Last Update:

Vinicius Junior has signed a new six-year contract at Real Madrid, ending speculation linking the Brazil forward with a move to Arsenal.

In a statement confirming the deal on Thursday, the La Liga club called the 26-year-old “one of the most important players in one of the most successful periods in our history”.

The two-time Champions League winner’s future had been under scrutiny because his previous contract expired in 2027.

Table of Contents

Vinicius Junior transfer news: What the forward said

Vinicius Junior said on Tuesday that new head coach Jose Mourinho had told him his expectations during gruelling training sessions after the forward’s return from the World Cup with Brazil.

Mourinho met Vinicius Junior on Monday for the first time since the Portuguese’s reappointment in May for a second tenure at the club.

“Very well,” the 26-year-old replied when Madrid’s official channel asked how he felt, sitting on a ball and smiling.

“[I’m] getting to know the new manager, the new players and working really hard. He wants me to be just as I’ve always been: happy, positive and playing. We all finished completely dead on our feet.”

Vinicius Jr: Real Madrid forward jilts Arsenal

Arsenal head coach Mikel Arteta has long been linked with a move for Vinicius Junior, smiling broadly but dodging the question when he was repeatedly asked about a potential bid after his side’s friendly win at Girona on Saturday.

Mourinho voiced worries over the lack of training time he will have with key senior players including Vinicius Junior after his team’s draw with Fiorentina on the same day, saying he would “like to have three weeks” with him.

Madrid’s enthusiastic coverage of Vinicius Junior’s return perhaps emphasised that the 15-time European champions were expecting him to stay.

The club posted footage of both of Vinicius Junior’s first sessions preparing for the 2026/27 season, titling the second “Vini Jr is back!” in capital letters.

Vinicius Junior: What Arsenal said

Arteta said Arsenal are “very active, trying to improve and evolve the team”. “That’s clear,” added the Spaniard.

“We expect to have movements in the next few weeks because we want to get better, like anybody else.

“You can just see the transfer market and our opponents and what they are doing. We are very ambitious with what we want to do.

“The margins are very small and if we want to get better, the level is going to increase. We need to increase the competition internally.

“We need to make sure that we identify the things we don’t have in the team to have bigger margins. That’s the way we have to think.

“We have even more responsibility and ambition than before. We know what is ahead; we know the qualities and capacity we have to compete with any team, but we need to prove that we belong at this level [of champions] now.”

Vinicius Jr stats: Best FIFA, La Liga, Champions League

Signed from Flamengo for a reported fee of around £39.4 million in 2018, Vinicius Junior’s individual honours include the 2023/24 Champions League Player of the Season award and the 2024 Best FIFA Men’s Player honour.

He was the Ballon d’Or runner up to Rodri in the same year. Here’s a look at the trophies Vinicius Junior has won with Madrid.

Real Madrid schedule: When does Vinicius Junior’s season start?

Madrid’s competitive season starts away to Espanyol on August 22 (20:30 BST). Arsenal kick off a day earlier at home to Coventry City (20:00).

articles.title: Newcastle boss Jaissle reveals Guimaraes future decided before he arrived
articles.summary: New Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle says he did not have a choice on Bruno Guimaraes' future.
articles.content:
Newcastle boss Jaissle reveals Guimaraes future decided before he arrived

New Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle says he did not have a choice on Bruno Guimaraes' future.

Last Update:

Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle has admitted Bruno Guimaraes’ departure was already decided before the pair held their first conversation, with the midfielder closing in on a £75 million move to Arsenal.

The Brazilian is expected to complete his long-awaited switch to the Gunners after the two clubs finally reached an agreement, ending his three-year spell at St James’ Park.

Jaissle revealed he only had a brief opportunity to speak with Guimaraes during Newcastle’s training camp in Spain before the midfielder said his goodbyes to team-mates and staff.

“I met him quickly, but the decision was already made,” Jaissle said.

“It was a nice conversation. He’s a fantastic player and a great human being. It’s tough but for him now it’s the next challenge and we need to deal with it at a later stage.

“We trust the players who are here already, but we will also see some changes.”

Guimaraes is set to become the latest high-profile departure from Newcastle, following Anthony Gordon’s move to Barcelona, Sandro Tonali’s switch to Tottenham and Alexander Isak’s transfer to Liverpool over the past year.

Jaissle determined to kickstart new era

Despite the loss of several key players, Jaissle insists Newcastle must embrace the opportunity to begin a new era.

“This is a challenge and there are so many transitions at the moment,” he said.

“Many big players left – legends of the club – but we need to see it as a chance.

“Not having too many excuses now, just thinking forward about what we can influence.

“Control the controllables, I used to say, and I’m sure there will be progress this season.”

The Magpies have already spent around £146 million this summer, focusing on young talent from across Europe.

Goalkeepers Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen, midfielders Aladji Bamba and Sean Steur, and winger Bazoumana Toure have all arrived, with 24-year-old Hornicek the oldest of the club’s new signings.

Jaissle, who previously enjoyed successful spells with RB Salzburg and Al-Ahli, believes he is ready for his first experience in the Premier League.

“This is something I don’t have on my CV, but that’s normal in football,” he said.

“At one point it has to be your first step and I’m now at that moment after being successful in Saudi Arabia and Austria.

“Everyone was dreaming about being a part of the Premier League and now here we are.”

Newcastle begin their 2026-27 Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool on August 23.

articles.summary: Uruguay legend Diego Forlan is the national team's new head coach
articles.content:
Uruguay: World Cup ‘idol’ Diego Forlan named new Celeste manager

Uruguay legend Diego Forlan is the national team's new head coach

Last Update:

Diego Forlan has been named the new head coach of the Uruguay national team following Marcelo Bielsa’s exit in June.

The Celeste failed to advance from the World Cup 2026 group stage, drawing with Saudi Arabia and Cape Verde and losing to Spain.

A Uruguayan FA statement called Forlan “one of the most important figures” in their history, adding that the 47-year-old will also take over the Under-20 team.

La vuelta de la leyenda 😉 pic.twitter.com/cllfYv4aLC

Diego Forlan: Uruguay FA full statement

“Forlan returns to where he left an indelible mark,” added the FA of the 2010 World Cup top scorer and Golden Ball winner.

“A role model, icon, and emblem of an unforgettable generation, the best player of the 2010 South Africa World Cup returns now to contribute his experience, leadership, and profound knowledge of international football from a technical position.

“The new coach will begin working immediately with the under-20 team. There, he will lead a project aimed at developing young talent, supporting their growth, and strengthening their path to the senior national team.

“His first challenge at the helm of the senior national team will come during the September-October international window, when Uruguay plays its FIFA friendly matches. It will mark the beginning of a new era, with one of its greatest idols once again at the helm.

“Having scored 36 goals in 112 appearances for Uruguay, won the Copa America in 2011 and played a decisive role in the historic fourth-place finish in South Africa, Forlan understands the meaning of representing his country like few others.

“His return reaffirms the [association’s] identity, ambition and commitment to a project that combines training, experience, and a strong sense of belonging.”

Diego Forlan’s first game in charge will come against Japan on September 24, before facing South Korea four days later on September 28.
